  "insights": [
   "AI-driven growth in Korea, Taiwan, and Vietnam is expected to remain robust in 2027, exceeding Bloomberg consensus estimates despite a moderation in global AI investment growth.",
   "Economic spillovers from the AI boom are diverging; Taiwan and Korea benefit from tech exports and capex, while Vietnam relies on government capex and FDI linked to supply chain shifts.",
   "Private consumption in Korea faces structural headwinds including aging demographics, negative wealth effects from equity/housing market corrections, and weak credit growth, limiting the positive impact of the AI boom.",
   "Inflation is projected to moderate to 2% by mid-2027 in Korea and Taiwan, supported by monetary tightening, currency appreciation, and price stability measures.",
   "Current account surpluses are at record highs in Taiwan (24% of GDP in 2026) and Korea (20.5% of GDP in 2026), with further appreciation pressure expected on the KRW due to high local currency needs for wages, taxes, and dividends.",
   "Monetary policy is expected to tighten through 1H 2027, with terminal rates reaching 3.5% in Korea and 2.375% in Taiwan, while Vietnam remains on hold.",
   "FX appreciation is viewed as a more effective and less damaging tool for disinflation than aggressive rate hikes, particularly in Korea where real interest rates are already restrictive."
